newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS-Gencor goes global, listing Billiton.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Gencor goes global, listing Billiton.

text.p: South African mining house Gencor Ltd on Wednesday unveiled plans to flex its global investment muscles by listing its base metals group Billiton Plc in London and raise $1 billion in an international equity placement.

Gencor, South Africa's second largest mining group, said Billiton would be able to raise far larger sums in London than it could from a South African base and had already received exchange control approval from the South African Reserve Bank.

"Billiton will be one of the largest and lowest cost producers of aluminium and the leading producer of ferroalloys, the world's largest exporter of thermal coal and a leading source of titanium minerals," the group said.

The company said it would follow international corporate models by grouping its precious metals interests under the Johannesburg-based Gencor umbrella to focus, in particular, on its global gold aspirations.

"There is no model of gold mining leadership within a diversified commodity portfolio and Gencor management felt it was essential to focus the two different businesses," said chairman Brian Gilbertson.

Gencor's plan -- which will see Billiton traded in London from August -- reflects a growing trend by South African mining houses to tap international markets to compete with Australian and North American rivals.
Gilbertson said the company had missed opportunities in the past because it had not had full access to international capital markets.

The move comes hot on the heels of the announcement of plans by gold exploration company Randgold Resources Ltd to raise up to $161 million by listing seven million shares on the London bourse to help fund existing and new projects.

The transfer of Gencor's non-precious metals interests to the Billiton company will be effected through the issue of three Billiton shares and one letter of entitlement for every four Gencor shares held by existing Gencor shareholders.
The market welcomed the news and Gencor's shares rose to a new year high of 21.10 rand, before slipping back to 20.75 rand, a gain of 165 cents on the day.

The new Gencor will consist of major South African assets such as Beatrix Mines Ltd, the lowest cost gold producer in the world, Oryx Gold Holdings Ltd and St Helena Gold Mines Ltd in the southern Free State province, Evander Gold Mines Ltd in Mpumalanga province and Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd.

Billiton, which took its 137-year-old name from a tin-rich island in the Indonesian archipelago, would hold major assets including Gencor's holding in Samancor Ltd, Alusaf, Richards Bay Minerals, Ingwe Coal Corp and its nickel interests.

Also on Wednesday Gencor sealed a deal with Australia's QNI Ltd to merge their nickel operations. According to a QNI statement, opportunities from the merger include the expansion of Gencor's Cerro Matoso nickel mine in Colombia and significant cuts to nickel production costs per pound.
The deal will eventually be registered in Billiton's name.
South African mining houses, concerned about ageing mines at home, have also increasingly been turning their eyes to investment opportunities abroad.
Earlier in June Gencor said it was looking at possible projects in Mozambique, Venezuela, Brazil, Colombia and Australia.
